A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SemanticDraw and contain readable main texts and supplementary material. The equations, algorithms, tables, and figures can be matched across revisions, including renumbered appendix content.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation evaluations, stabilization and throughput ablations in Tables 1–6, and qualitative regional-generation and panorama results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds user preferences, an LRDiff comparison, centering-step sensitivity results, and a streaming-consistency demonstration.

M1.justification: Section S3.1 introduces an optional streaming mode that shares noise tensors across successive generations for consistent incremental editing. v3 describes adjustable seed control but not this stream-wide reuse. The core stabilization method and Algorithms S1–S2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage remains COCO-based regional image generation, large canvases and panoramas, and interactive semantic drawing. The added preference assessment, comparator example, and generation-control comparisons evaluate these retained tasks; they do not establish a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Figure S5 newly compares SemanticDraw against LRDiff and LRDiff combined with LCM. This is a limited qualitative comparator extension; the MultiDiffusion comparisons in the retained quantitative tables are unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds human preference assessment in Table 7, a sweep over one to four centering steps in Figure S2, and fixed versus unfixed noise under the same interactive-control sequence in Figure S11. Existing COCO evaluation settings remain unchanged. Participant counts and detailed user-study procedures are not supplied.

E4.justification: The existing component, throughput, and mask-blur analyses are retained. v4 adds a centering-duration sensitivity example examining composition and boundary artifacts, plus a case study comparing consistency across streaming outputs with and without seed fixing.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new seed-fixing comparison concerns an inference control, rather than repeated-run or statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results. New results include preferences of 90.9% for SemanticDraw, 9.1% for MultiDiffusion, and 0.0% for MultiDiffusion+LCM; Figure S5 reports 45s, 1s, and 1s for LRDiff, LRDiff+LCM, and SemanticDraw. v4 also adds centering and streaming-consistency findings and attributes approximately 40% of runtime to text encoding.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the appendix mask definition (S7), and Algorithms S1–S2 are retained. The new centering discussion is empirical and explanatory; no mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of acceleration-compatible regional control, model- and scheduler-agnostic operation, multi-prompt streaming, sub-second generation, and up to approximately 50-fold acceleration. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section S1.3 explains how excessive centering can disrupt late-stage boundary formation and image harmony, and discusses the fidelity–harmony trade-off. v4 also links center bias to training-image composition and explains how shared noise supports consistent editing sessions.

D1.justification: Section 5 clarifies existing text-embedding caching and reports its runtime contribution. Section S3.1 specifies noise-tensor sharing and states that the seed-fixing option is available in the code. Core hardware, launch instructions, and algorithm details remain; the two-step centering setting is confirmed rather than changed.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion of SSI, LazyDiffusion, Differential Diffusion, Mixture of Diffusers, and LRDiff, refining comparisons involving architecture, latency, overlapping regions, and noise addition. It also adds a LAION-400M citation and removes the Hinton distillation reference. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion, and application explanation receive targeted rewrites. v4 adds a fidelity–harmony subsection and acknowledgment and revises several headings. The overall narrative order and most method and experiment prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual exposition is substantially revised: Figure 4 redraws the pipeline and explicitly displays the text-embedding cache, while Figure 5 simplifies mask processing. Table 7 and Figures S2, S5, and S11 add new evidence displays. Existing appendix figures are retained across renumbering and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v4 improves explanation and practical guidance through revised diagrams, centering-sensitivity evidence, and the fixed-noise editing demonstration. The LRDiff example modestly broadens empirical support while existing benchmark results remain intact. These gains are limited: the new user study lacks participant counts and procedures, and the additional qualitative examples do not establish broad reliability.
